NASB.1: When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go as at other times to seek omens but he set his face toward the wilderness.
NASB.2: And Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel camping tribe by tribe; and the Spirit of God came upon him.
NASB.3: He took up his discourse and said, 'The oracle of Balaam the son of Beor, And the oracle of the man whose eye is opened;
NASB.4: The oracle of him who hears the words of God, Who sees the vision of the Almighty, Falling down, yet having his eyes uncovered,
NASB.5: How fair are your tents, O Jacob, Your dwellings, O Israel!
NASB.6: 'Like valleys that stretch out, Like gardens beside the river, Like aloes planted by the LORD, Like cedars beside the waters.
NASB.7: 'Water will flow from his buckets, And his seed [will be] by many waters, And his king shall be higher than Agag, And his kingdom shall be exalted.
NASB.8: 'God brings him out of Egypt, He is for him like the horns of the wild ox. He will devour the nations [who are] his adversaries, And will crush their bones in pieces, And shatter [them] with his arrows.
NASB.9: 'He couches, he lies down as a lion, And as a lion, who dares rouse him? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, And cursed is everyone who curses you.'
NASB.10: Then Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together; and Balak said to Balaam, 'I called you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have persisted in blessing them these three times!
NASB.11: 'Therefore, flee to your place now. I said I would honor you greatly, but behold, the LORD has held you back from honor.'
NASB.12: Balaam said to Balak, 'Did I not tell your messengers whom you had sent to me, saying,
NASB.13: 'Though Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything contrary to the command of the LORD, either good or bad, of my own accord. What the LORD speaks, that I will speak '?
NASB.14: 'And now, behold, I am going to my people; come, [and] I will advise you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.'
NASB.15: He took up his discourse and said, 'The oracle of Balaam the son of Beor, And the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
NASB.16: The oracle of him who hears the words of God, And knows the knowledge of the Most High, Who sees the vision of the Almighty, Falling down, yet having his eyes uncovered.
NASB.17: 'I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near; A star shall come forth from Jacob, A scepter shall rise from Israel, And shall crush through the forehead of Moab, And tear down all the sons of Sheth.
NASB.18: 'Edom shall be a possession, Seir, its enemies, also will be a possession, While Israel performs valiantly.
NASB.19: 'One from Jacob shall have dominion, And will destroy the remnant from the city.'
NASB.20: And he looked at Amalek and took up his discourse and said, 'Amalek was the first of the nations, But his end [shall be] destruction.'
NASB.21: And he looked at the Kenite, and took up his discourse and said, 'Your dwelling place is enduring, And your nest is set in the cliff.
NASB.22: 'Nevertheless Kain will be consumed; How long will Asshur keep you captive?'
NASB.23: Then he took up his discourse and said, 'Alas, who can live except God has ordained it?
NASB.24: 'But ships [shall come] from the coast of Kittim, And they shall afflict Asshur and will afflict Eber; So they also [will come] to destruction.'
NASB.25: Then Balaam arose and departed and returned to his place, and Balak also went his way.

ESV.1: When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go, as at other times, to look for omens, but set his face toward the wilderness.
ESV.2: And Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel camping tribe by tribe. And the Spirit of God came upon him,
ESV.3: and he took up his discourse and said, “The oracle of Balaam the son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
ESV.4: the oracle of him who hears the words of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down with his eyes uncovered:
ESV.5: How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your encampments, O Israel!
ESV.6: Like palm groves  that stretch afar, like gardens beside a river, like aloes that the LORD has planted, like cedar trees beside the waters.
ESV.7: Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters; his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.
ESV.8: God brings him out of Egypt and is for him like the horns of the wild ox; he shall eat up the nations, his adversaries, and shall break their bones in pieces and pierce them through with his arrows.
ESV.9: He crouched, he lay down like a lion and like a lioness; who will rouse him up? Blessed are those who bless you, and cursed are those who curse you.”
ESV.10: And Balak's anger was kindled against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. And Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them these three times.
ESV.11: Therefore now flee to your own place. I said, ‘I will certainly honor you,’ but the LORD has held you back from honor.”
ESV.12: And Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not tell your messengers whom you sent to me,
ESV.13: ‘If Balak should give me his house full of silver and gold, I would not be able to go beyond the word of the LORD, to do either good or bad of my own will. What the LORD speaks, that will I speak’?
ESV.14: And now, behold, I am going to my people. Come, I will let you know what this people will do to your people in the latter days.”
ESV.15: And he took up his discourse and said, “The oracle of Balaam the son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
ESV.16: the oracle of him who hears the words of God, and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down with his eyes uncovered:
ESV.17: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near: a star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel; it shall crush the forehead  of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.
ESV.18: Edom shall be dispossessed; Seir also, his enemies, shall be dispossessed. Israel is doing valiantly.
ESV.19: And one from Jacob shall exercise dominion and destroy the survivors of cities!”
ESV.20: Then he looked on Amalek and took up his discourse and said, “Amalek was the first among the nations, but its end is utter destruction.”
ESV.21: And he looked on the Kenite, and took up his discourse and said, “Enduring is your dwelling place, and your nest is set in the rock.
ESV.22: Nevertheless, Kain shall be burned when Asshur takes you away captive.”
ESV.23: And he took up his discourse and said, “Alas, who shall live when God does this?
ESV.24: But ships shall come from Kittim and shall afflict Asshur and Eber; and he too shall come to utter destruction.”
ESV.25: Then Balaam rose and went back to his place. And Balak also went his way.

WEB.1: When Balaam saw that it pleased Yahweh to bless Israel, he didn’t go, as at the other times, to meet with enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
WEB.2: Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel dwelling according to their tribes; and the Spirit of God came on him.
WEB.3: He took up his parable, and said, “Balaam the son of Beor says, the man whose eyes are open says;
WEB.4: he says, who hears the words of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, falling down, and having his eyes open:
WEB.5: How goodly are your tents, Jacob, and your tents, Israel!
WEB.6: As valleys they are spread out, as gardens by the riverside, as aloes which Yahweh has planted, as cedar trees beside the waters.
WEB.7: Water shall flow from his buckets. His seed shall be in many waters. His king shall be higher than Agag. His kingdom shall be exalted.
WEB.8: God brings him out of Egypt. He has as it were the strength of the wild ox. He shall eat up the nations his adversaries, shall break their bones in pieces, and pierce them with his arrows.
WEB.9: He couched, he lay down as a lion, as a lioness; who shall rouse him up? Everyone who blesses you is blessed. Everyone who curses you is cursed.”
WEB.10: Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and, behold, you have altogether blessed them these three times.
WEB.11: Therefore now flee you to your place! I thought to promote you to great honor; but, behold, Yahweh has kept you back from honor.”
WEB.12: Balaam said to Balak, “Didn’t I also tell your messengers who you sent to me, saying,
WEB.13: ‘If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I can’t go beyond Yahweh’s word, to do either good or bad of my own mind. I will say what Yahweh says’?
WEB.14: Now, behold, I go to my people. Come, I will inform you what this people shall do to your people in the latter days.”
WEB.15: He took up his parable, and said, “Balaam the son of Beor says, the man whose eyes are open says;
WEB.16: he says, who hears the words of God, knows the knowledge of the Most High, and who sees the vision of the Almighty, Falling down, and having his eyes open:
WEB.17: I see him, but not now. I see him, but not near. A star will come out of Jacob. A scepter will rise out of Israel, and shall strike through the corners of Moab, and break down all the sons of Sheth.
WEB.18: Edom shall be a possession. Seir, his enemies, also shall be a possession, while Israel does valiantly.
WEB.19: Out of Jacob shall one have dominion, and shall destroy the remnant from the city.”
WEB.20: He looked at Amalek, and took up his parable, and said, “Amalek was the first of the nations, But his latter end shall come to destruction.”
WEB.21: He looked at the Kenite, and took up his parable, and said, “Your dwelling place is strong. Your nest is set in the rock.
WEB.22: Nevertheless Kain shall be wasted, until Asshur carries you away captive.”
WEB.23: He took up his parable, and said, “Alas, who shall live when God does this?

WEB.25: Balaam rose up, and went and returned to his place; and Balak also went his way.

AMP.1: When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go as he had done each time before [superstitiously] to seek omens and signs [in the natural world], but he set his face toward the wilderness (desert).
AMP.2: And Balaam raised his eyes and he saw Israel living in their tents tribe by tribe; and the Spirit of God came on him.
AMP.3:
He took up his [third] discourse (oracle) and said:
"The oracle of Balaam the son of Beor,
And the oracle of the man whose eye is opened [at last, to see clearly the purpose and will of God],
AMP.4:
The oracle of one who hears the words of God,
Who sees the vision of the Almighty,
Falling down, but having his eyes open and uncovered,
AMP.5:
How fair are your tents, O Jacob,
And your tabernacles, O Israel!
AMP.6:
"Like valleys that stretch out,
Like gardens beside the river,
Like aloes planted by the LORD,
Like cedars beside the waters.
AMP.7:
"Water [that is, great blessings] will flow from his buckets,
And his offspring will live by many waters,
And his king will be higher than Agag,
And his kingdom shall be exalted.
AMP.8:
"God brought Israel out of Egypt;
Israel has strength like the wild ox;
He will devour [Gentile] nations, his adversaries (enemies),
And will crush their bones in pieces,
And shatter them with his arrows.
AMP.9:
"He bowed down [to rest], he lies down as a lion;
And as a lioness, who dares to rouse him?
Blessed [of God] is he who blesses you,
And cursed [of God] is he who curses you."
AMP.10: Then Balak's anger was kindled against Balaam, and he struck his hands together; and Balak said to Balaam, "I called you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have done nothing but bless them these three times.
AMP.11: Therefore now flee to your place! I had intended to honor you greatly, but behold, the LORD has held you back from honor."
AMP.12: Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not tell your messengers whom you had sent to me,
AMP.13: 'Even if Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD, to do either good or bad of my own accord. What the LORD speaks, that I will speak?'
AMP.14: And now, look, I am going to my people; come, I will advise you as to what this people [Israel] will do to your people [Moab] in the days to come."
AMP.15:
He took up his [fourth] discourse (oracle) and said:
"The oracle of Balaam the son of Beor,
The oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
AMP.16:
The oracle of him who hears the words of God
And knows the knowledge of the Most High,
Who sees the vision of the Almighty,
Falling down, but having his eyes open and uncovered:
AMP.17:
"I see Him, but not now;
I behold Him, but not near.
A star shall come forth from [the descendants of] Jacob,
A scepter shall rise out of [the descendants of] Israel
And shall crush the forehead of Moab
And destroy all the sons of Sheth.
AMP.18:
"Edom shall be [taken as] a possession,
[Mount] Seir, Israel's enemies, also will be a possession,
While Israel performs valiantly.
AMP.19:
"One from [the descendants of] Jacob shall have dominion
And will destroy the remnant from the city."
AMP.20:
Balaam looked at Amalek and took up his [fifth] discourse (oracle) and said:
"Amalek was the first of the [neighboring] nations [to oppose the Israelites after they left Egypt],
But his end shall be destruction."
AMP.21:
And Balaam looked at the Kenites and took up his [sixth] discourse (oracle) and said:
"Strong is your dwelling place,
And you set your nest in the cliff.
AMP.22:
"Nevertheless the Kenites will be consumed.
How long will Asshur (Assyria) keep you (Israel) captive?"
AMP.23:
Then he took up his [seventh] discourse (oracle) and said:
"Alas, who can live unless God has ordained it?
AMP.24:
"But ships shall come from the coast of Kittim,
And shall afflict Asshur (Assyria) and Eber;
So they (the victors) also will come to destruction."
AMP.25: Then Balaam arose and departed and returned to his place, and Balak also went on his way.

NLT.1: By now Balaam realized that the LORD was determined to bless Israel, so he did not resort to divination as before. Instead, he turned and looked out toward the wilderness,
NLT.2: where he saw the people of Israel camped, tribe by tribe. Then the Spirit of God came upon him,
NLT.3:
and this is the message he delivered: “This is the message of Balaam son of Beor,
the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
NLT.4:
the message of one who hears the words of God,
who sees a vision from the Almighty,
who bows down with eyes wide open:
NLT.5:
How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob;
how lovely are your homes, O Israel!
NLT.6:
They spread before me like palm groves,
like gardens by the riverside.
They are like tall trees planted by the LORD,
like cedars beside the waters.
NLT.7:
Water will flow from their buckets;
their offspring have all they need.
Their king will be greater than Agag;
their kingdom will be exalted.
NLT.8:
God brought them out of Egypt;
for them he is as strong as a wild ox.
He devours all the nations that oppose him,
breaking their bones in pieces,
shooting them with arrows.
NLT.9:
Like a lion, Israel crouches and lies down;
like a lioness, who dares to arouse her?
Blessed is everyone who blesses you, O Israel,
and cursed is everyone who curses you.”
NLT.10: King Balak flew into a rage against Balaam. He angrily clapped his hands and shouted, “I called you to curse my enemies! Instead, you have blessed them three times.
NLT.11: Now get out of here! Go back home! I promised to reward you richly, but the LORD has kept you from your reward.”
NLT.12: Balaam told Balak, “Don’t you remember what I told your messengers? I said,
NLT.13: ‘Even if Balak were to give me his palace filled with silver and gold, I would be powerless to do anything against the will of the LORD.’ I told you that I could say only what the LORD says!
NLT.14: Now I am returning to my own people. But first let me tell you what the Israelites will do to your people in the future.”
NLT.15:
This is the message Balaam delivered: “This is the message of Balaam son of Beor,
the message of the man whose eyes see clearly,
NLT.16:
the message of one who hears the words of God,
who has knowledge from the Most High,
who sees a vision from the Almighty,
who bows down with eyes wide open:
NLT.17:
I see him, but not here and now.
I perceive him, but far in the distant future.
A star will rise from Jacob;
a scepter will emerge from Israel.
It will crush the heads of Moab’s people,
cracking the skulls of the people of Sheth.
NLT.18:
Edom will be taken over,
and Seir, its enemy, will be conquered,
while Israel marches on in triumph.
NLT.19:
A ruler will rise in Jacob
who will destroy the survivors of Ir.”
NLT.20:
Then Balaam looked over toward the people of Amalek and delivered this message: “Amalek was the greatest of nations,
but its destiny is destruction!”
NLT.21:
Then he looked over toward the Kenites and delivered this message: “Your home is secure;
your nest is set in the rocks.
NLT.22:
But the Kenites will be destroyed
when Assyria takes you captive.”
NLT.23:
Balaam concluded his messages by saying: “Alas, who can survive
unless God has willed it?
NLT.24:
Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus ;
they will oppress Assyria and afflict Eber,
but they, too, will be utterly destroyed.”
NLT.25: Then Balaam left and returned home, and Balak also went on his way.

NET.1: When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go as at the other times to seek for omens, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
NET.2: When Balaam lifted up his eyes, he saw Israel camped tribe by tribe; and the Spirit of God came upon him.
NET.3: Then he uttered this oracle: “The oracle of Balaam son of Beor; the oracle of the man whose eyes are open;
NET.4: the oracle of the one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, although falling flat on the ground with eyes open:
NET.5: ‘How beautiful are your tents, O Jacob, and your dwelling places, O Israel!
NET.6: They are like valleys stretched forth, like gardens by the river’s side, like aloes that the LORD has planted, and like cedar trees beside the waters.
NET.7: He will pour the water out of his buckets, and their descendants will be like abundant water; their king will be greater than Agag, and their kingdom will be exalted.
NET.8: God brought them out of Egypt. They have, as it were, the strength of a young bull; they will devour hostile people and will break their bones and will pierce them through with arrows.
NET.9: They crouch and lie down like a lion, and as a lioness, who can stir him? Blessed is the one who blesses you, and cursed is the one who curses you!’”
NET.10: Then Balak became very angry at Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and look, you have done nothing but bless them these three times!
NET.11: So now, go back where you came from! I said that I would greatly honor you; but now the LORD has stood in the way of your honor.”
NET.12: Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not also tell your messengers whom you sent to me,
NET.13: ‘If Balak would give me his palace full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the commandment of the LORD to do either good or evil of my own will, but whatever the LORD tells me I must speak’?
NET.14: And now, I am about to go back to my own people. Come now, and I will advise you as to what this people will do to your people in the future.”
NET.15: Then he uttered this oracle: “The oracle of Balaam son of Beor; the oracle of the man whose eyes are open;
NET.16: the oracle of the one who hears the words of God, and who knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, although falling flat on the ground with eyes open:
NET.17: ‘I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not close at hand. A star will march forth out of Jacob, and a scepter will rise out of Israel. He will crush the skulls of Moab, and the heads of all the sons of Sheth.
NET.18: Edom will be a possession, Seir, his enemies, will also be a possession; but Israel will act valiantly.
NET.19: A ruler will be established from Jacob; he will destroy the remains of the city.’”
NET.20: Then Balaam looked on Amalek and delivered this oracle: “Amalek was the first of the nations, but his end will be that he will perish.”
NET.21: Then he looked on the Kenites and uttered this oracle: “Your dwelling place seems strong, and your nest is set on a rocky cliff.
NET.22: Nevertheless the Kenite will be consumed. How long will Asshur take you away captive?”
NET.23: Then he uttered this oracle: “O, who will survive when God does this!
NET.24: Ships will come from the coast of Kittim, and will afflict Asshur, and will afflict Eber, and he will also perish forever.”
NET.25: Balaam got up and departed and returned to his home, and Balak also went his way.
